title: Eureka!
intro: [excited] Safety goggles ON, everybody! Tonight we're celebrating Disney's brilliant inventors, mad scientists and gadgets that go boom. [laughs] Results may vary. Explosions likely.

art.prompt: A cluttered inventor's laboratory bursting with bubbling beakers, sparking coils, blueprints, gears, a glowing lightbulb and a tiny rocket on a workbench Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

categories.title: San Fransokyo Science
categories.intro: Our film category is Big Hero 6! [chuckles] Are you satisfied with your care?

art.prompt: A futuristic hilly city at sunset blending a giant red suspension bridge with pagoda-style rooftops, wind turbines floating like blimps above the skyline Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: Baymax asks patients to rate their pain on a scale of 1 to this number.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is 10! [laughs] Hiro rates being bumped by a robot a zero.

clues.clue: Hiro's caring older brother, who invented Baymax.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Tadashi! [sighs] His motto: look for a new angle.

clues.clue: Hiro's swarms of tiny magnetic robots, controlled by a neural headband, are called these.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is microbots! The only limit is your imagination. And your villain's.

clues.clue: This Big Hero 6 member is a neat freak who fights with laser-induction plasma blades.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Wasabi! [chuckles] He has a place for everything, and everything in its place.

clues.clue: In Big Hero 6's post-credits scene, Stan Lee appears as the father of this team member.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Fred! [gasps] Turns out Fred's dad is a retired superhero. Of course he is.

categories.title: Mad Scientists and Bright Ideas
categories.intro: Our themed category: Disney's most memorable inventors. [excited] Keep moving forward!

art.prompt: A row of eccentric inventions on a sunny workbench: a steam-powered wood chopper, a bouncing green goo jar, a sandwich-launching contraption and a brass time-machine dial Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: Belle's father, an eccentric inventor, gets lost on his way to the fair in Beauty and the Beast.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Maurice! [laughs] His wood-chopping machine only explodes sometimes.

clues.clue: Meet the Robinsons' inventor family lives by this motto, the title of Walt Disney's favorite saying.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is keep moving forward! The film ends with Walt's real quote on screen.

clues.clue: Meet the Robinsons' villain, Bowler Hat Guy, is really Lewis's sleepy former orphanage roommate, nicknamed this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Goob! He stayed awake once, and missed the catch of his life.

clues.clue: In 1997's Flubber, Robin Williams plays absent-minded professor Philip Brainard, who teaches at this college.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Medfield College! The same school from the 1961 original. Bounce on over!

clues.clue: This actor played Professor Ned Brainard, inventor of flubber, in 1961's The Absent-Minded Professor.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Fred MacMurray! He drove a flying Model T to prove flubber works.

categories.title: Inventor's Workbench
categories.intro: It's a picture category! I'll show you a famous invention. [whispers] You name the Disney movie.

clues.clue: This invention comes from which Disney movie?
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Flubber! Flying rubber. It bounces higher every time.

clues.clue: This invention comes from which Disney movie?
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Honey, I Shrunk the Kids! [laughs] Wayne Szalinski's shrink ray, plus one stray baseball.

clues.clue: This invention comes from which Disney movie?
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Beauty and the Beast! Maurice's wood chopper, a real crowd pleaser at the fair.

clues.clue: This invention comes from which Disney movie?
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Meet the Robinsons! [excited] A time machine, built by a kid, borrowed by a guy in a bowler hat.

categories.title: Science Fair
categories.intro: Our Parks category: science and the future at the parks. [chuckles] Show your work.

art.prompt: A futuristic world's fair with a towering spire, a white plastic house of the future, a giant centrifuge, glowing greenhouses and molecule sculptures Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: At EPCOT's Mission: SPACE, guests train to become these.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is astronauts! [excited] Mission Control, we have a snack break.

clues.clue: The 3D show Honey, I Shrunk the Audience played at EPCOT in this pavilion, home of Figment.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is the Imagination! pavilion. It ran there from 1994 to 2010.

clues.clue: Disneyland's Monsanto House of the Future, from 1957 to 1967, was built almost entirely from this material.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is plastic! [laughs] When they tore it down, the wrecking ball bounced right off.

clues.clue: Mission: SPACE uses these spinning machines to create the G-forces of a rocket launch.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is centrifuges! [gasps] That's why there's a green team and an orange team.

clues.clue: Disneyland's 1967 attraction Adventure Thru Inner Space shrank guests in Atomobiles down to the size of this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is an atom! Riders passed through a snowflake and into the atom itself.

categories.title: Duckburg Brainiacs
categories.intro: Our fan category: the brilliant minds of Duckburg. [excited] Woo-oo!

art.prompt: A cluttered inventor's workshop inside a tall old water tower, lightbulbs everywhere, a robotic suit on a stand and blueprints pinned to the walls Original illustration, 16:9, rich saturated colors, cinematic lighting, no people, no characters, no text, no logos.

clues.clue: This chicken inventor is Duckburg's resident genius in DuckTales.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Gyro Gearloose! [chuckles] His inventions work perfectly, about half the time.

clues.clue: Gyro's tiny robot assistant has a lightbulb for a head and is called this.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Little Helper! Small, silent and smarter than most of us.

clues.clue: In the original DuckTales, Gyro builds this armored robotic suit for Scrooge's accountant, Fenton Crackshell.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Gizmoduck! [laughs] Blathering blatherskite!

clues.clue: This brainy, German-accented scientist duck, Donald's uncle, debuted on TV in 1961.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Ludwig Von Drake! He debuted on Walt Disney's Wonderful World of Color.

clues.clue: This legendary Disney comic book artist created Gyro Gearloose in 1952.
clues.reveal: The correct answer is Carl Barks! The Good Duck Artist also created Scrooge McDuck and Duckburg.
